entities.summary:
The Red Eyebrows were a 1st-century AD rebellion against the Xin dynasty in China. 

The rebellion, led by a group of former soldiers, began in 17 CE and lasted for a decade. Its significance lies in its impact on the fragile stability of the early Han Dynasty, which was struggling to consolidate power after the downfall of the Xin. 

The Red Eyebrows were eventually suppressed in 27 CE, but not before they had caused significant damage to the imperial administration and army. 

The legacy of the Red Eyebrows can be seen in the subsequent reforms of Emperor Ming of Han, who sought to address the issues of corruption and inefficiency that the rebellion had exposed.
